summary: Rung 1 is six of seven done: build output, caches and repositories are classified, stored as single objects, never entered by the scanner, and the app now uses all of it. A scope of 1,080,000 entries behind objects scans in 0.7 seconds. TASK-614, the capacity guard, is the last task before GATE-619.
progress: RESEARCH-601 verified: detection rules chosen from a corpus measurement, not guesses. Name matching alone would have offered 29 tracked source directories for deletion.
CONTRACT-601 verified: object row shape, confidence vocabulary, never-classify and never-offer rules, sizing and staleness, reversible migration, each naming the task that proves it.
TASK-611 verified: the classifier, with tracked source refused before any other rule and optional repository answers so an unreadable repository decides nothing.

TASK-613 verified: schema 15 `current_objects`, plus a transactional, resumable, idempotent collapse. Two contract rules are database constraints. Migration 14 to 15 rehearsed with a working rollback.
TASK-612 verified: the scanner records an object and never enters it. 1,080,000 entries behind 12 objects complete one generation in 0.7 s with zero per-file rows inside an object.
TASK-615 verified (added by replan R2): the app wires the classifier into its probe and converges an installed store in bounded batches, reporting what it collapsed.
Replan R2 added TASK-615 after the gap was found: nothing wired the object model into the running app, so rung 1's claim would have been false on a real machine.

decisions.decision: TASK-612 was released and TASK-613 done first.
decisions.rationale: TASK-612's criterion requires object rows to be published, which needs the durable row that belongs to TASK-613. Doing them in that order kept both criteria honest.

decisions.decision: Wiring became its own task rather than being folded into an existing one.
decisions.rationale: No criterion covered constructing the scanner with a classifier or running the collapse in the app. Folding it in would have made a gate prove something it never named.

decisions.decision: The ancestor walk rejects non-absolute paths and is bounded at 256.
decisions.rationale: A non-absolute path made deletingLastPathComponent prepend '..' forever and hung a test for 30 minutes. Diagnosed from a stack sample, not guessed at.

decisions.decision: A discarded mutation was recorded rather than counted as a red.
decisions.rationale: Moving a checkpoint inside a transaction changed nothing observable; presenting it as a passing red would have overstated the evidence.

assumptions: Objects publish without aggregates until TASK-621 measures them; a missing size must never be read as zero.
The maintainer corpus is one machine; detection coverage elsewhere is unmeasured, which RESEARCH-601 states.
risks: The installed app on this machine is still 1.2.1 and still has the stuck scan. Nothing in this plan has been released; the fix exists only in the repository.
GATE-619 must converge a copy of a real installed store end to end. Every proof so far uses stores built in tests or synthetic fixtures.

Assurance currently reports ASSET-BUILD and ASSET-RESOURCE without a sufficient inspection, and four inspections stale from the last updates. Both are expected before a gate and are the gate's work to clear.
The opt-in scale case builds a million files. It refuses to run without a supervisor-owned fixture and its ownership token, but it is heavy: run it deliberately, never as part of an ordinary suite.
